extracted.intended_audience: Spanish royal officials, governors, viceroys, and colonial administrators (16th-century Manila/New Spain correspondence)
extracted.subtask_description: Directives, decrees, and recommendations for administering, pacifying, settling, and economically managing the Philippine islands (Luzon/Manila) addressed to the Spanish Crown and its colonial agents in the 1570s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate commerce and remit royal funds to Nueva España
rubrics_metrics.description: "orders should be sent to the governor of these islands charging him to strive most diligently to facilitate commerce, and take care that the moneys belonging to your Majesty be sent to the officials of Nueva España, in order that they may provide the islands with the supplies that will be needed, and which will be requested from here."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governor must actively promote and ease trade; ensure royal monies are forwarded to Nueva España officials who will provision the islands for war and other emergencies. This is framed as a necessary administrative step tied to fulfilling supply requests and wartime readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include maps and geographic intelligence in reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The governor sends a map of the island of Luçon and of the coast of the mainland of China; also a paper received from the Chinese with a map of the whole land of China, and promises of more detailed maps next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports to the Crown should include maps and geographic descriptions; procure and forward more detailed local and foreign (Chinese) maps as they become available to strengthen claims and planning for exploration and trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship and remit valuable local produce to royal officials
rubrics_metrics.description: "By the ship 'Spiritu Santo,' now about to sail, I am sending to your Majesty's officials in Mexico eighty quintals of cinnamon and forty-six quintals of wax."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export valuable commodities (cinnamon, wax, etc.) to Crown officials as part of provisioning/revenue. Log quantities and shipments in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an account of existing slaves and justifications for enslavement
rubrics_metrics.description: Per royal decree (Madrid, May 18, 1572) the governor is commanded to send an account of the slaves that exist in these parts; and how, and with what justification, they are slaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document categories and origins of enslaved persons, noting inherited slavery, war captives, punishment for crimes, enslavement for unpaid debts/loans, enslavement for petty theft, sale during famine, and other local customs that produce slavery. This is an administrative obligation to report to the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerate acceptable local grounds/circumstances leading to slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: The letter lists causes: born slaves (ancestral), captives in village wars, raids for booty (including against relatives), enslavement for small thefts (knife, sugar-cane, rice), being unable to prove testimony, punishment for crimes (murder, adultery, poisoning), sale during famine, and enslavement resulting from indebtedness where debts compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accounting for slaves, distinguish among these categories; the governor's report should acknowledge local customs and causes so the Crown can judge legality/justice under Spanish decrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid acquiring new slaves in Spanish-occupied areas; use preexisting local slave labor carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it be forbidden, in those places where the Spanish live, to acquire slaves in any shape or manner--those who were made slaves and were slaves before we came here and are slaves now, and whom the natives buy and sell among each other...without them this land cannot be preserved."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the Crown's prohibition on acquiring new slaves in Spanish areas while reporting the practical reliance on preexisting indigenous slave systems for maintaining the colony. Reports should reconcile royal policy with local realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return unlawfully seized foreigners and consider diplomatic consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: After seizing two Chinese junks and plundering goods, the governor had the Chinese returned, expressing regret and noting the harm to commerce: 'I was exceedingly sorry that such an injury should be inflicted... what grieves me most... is the news which the Chinese will carry to their own country about us.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seizures of foreign vessels/merchants harm trade; where possible return seized persons and goods and repair relations to restore commerce. Include diplomatic and commercial consequences in dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage settlement with married Spaniards and families
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: 'send all the married men who can possibly come... With the existence of settled communities the natives... will feel more secure' and arrival of women reassures natives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote colonization by sending married settlers and wives to foster stable communities, increase agriculture, and pacify/assimilate natives; report effects on native trust and service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send sufficient clergy (numbers and qualities specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to send forty or fifty friars — 'learned theologians of mature age and good life and habits' — plus Augustine religious (five monasteries) and a prelate (bishop/archbishop) 'of learning and of good life,' and secular clergy to serve as prebends, canons, and chaplains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious personnel should be mature, learned, and of good conduct; they are central to conversion efforts and instruction in the Catholic faith. Specify numbers and orders; include a superior prelate to oversee ecclesiastical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send a military force of five hundred soldiers and associated logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Request: 'May your Majesty please to send five hundred soldiers here, who may be posted in the said island of Luzon, so that by their help the said governor can subjugate and settle the said island of Luzon, and discover other neighboring islands.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a plan to transport and station 500 troops to secure, pacify, and enable further exploration/colonization. Include logistics and cost-minimizing proposals in the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-saving method for recruiting and transporting troops via España and Nueva España
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that troops be collected in España under pretext of convoy to Nueva España: of the usual 200 men, leave 100 behind and supply them from the 500; when arriving Nueva España, send troops to Acapulco to board the fleet from the islands — this would save between seven and eight thousand ducats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed recruitment and rotation scheme intended to minimize gratuities and transport cost; coordinate with existing fleets and passenger movements to avoid extra expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing troops' embarkation via Nueva España/Acapulco to coincide with returning fleet
rubrics_metrics.description: When the 500 men arrive in Nueva España they should go directly to Acapulco because it will be more than two months since the fleet from the island of Luzon will have arrived; troops can then be embarked immediately on that fleet to reach Luzon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronize troop movements with trans-Pacific fleet schedules (Vera Cruz -> Acapulco -> Pacific fleet) to ensure timely deployment and reduce idle time/costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send 50 skilled workmen (shipbuilders, locksmiths, blacksmiths) to build ships locally
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to send 'workmen, masters to build ships and galleys, locksmiths, and blacksmiths to the number of fifty.' Suggestion to supply these laborers by transferring negro slaves from Habana fortifications if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring skilled artisans to exploit local timber and materials to build 3–4 vessels per year, enabling regular voyages and exploration. Consider using available labor sources to staff projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a local shipbuilding program with annual production targets
rubrics_metrics.description: With fifty workmen and abundant wood and iron locally, 'the said workmen should build three or four vessels each year, so that the trip can be made from Nueva España to the said islands and return, with two fleets.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set concrete shipbuilding targets (3–4 vessels/year) to maintain trans-Pacific communication, exploration, and colonization; coordinate workmen, materials, and fleet schedules to meet targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate use of arriving soldiers for subjugation, settlement, and exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon arrival, the five hundred soldiers are to 'effect immediately the purpose for which they were brought--namely, to subjugate, settle, and explore both the said island of Luzon, and those regions nearest China: the Japans, the Lequios, and the island of Escauchu.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy troops promptly to achieve military and colonial objectives; combine military action with settlement and discovery missions targeting nearby strategic regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit royal officials from holding encomiendas; treat such holdings as royal property
rubrics_metrics.description: "it is an encumbrance and damage to the royal treasury for his Majesty's officials to hold encomiendas of Indians...as such, his Majesty has forbidden this...the governor ordered...that they shall not hold the said Indians in encomiendas...he retracted those which were granted them...he ordered the officials of the royal estate...that they shall hold those encomiendas as the royal property...make collections, and have the natives instructed in the tenets of our holy Catholic faith."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal officials must not personally possess encomiendas; any villages previously held by them are to be considered Crown property, administered for the royal treasury and for conversion/ instruction of natives. Duplicate acts sent to the Crown; officials charged in conscience and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability: sworn declarations of tributes collected and specified record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials (accountant, factor, treasurer) were required to declare, 'clearly and specifically, under oath, the amount thus collected, and for what persons and by whose hand it was collected,' and not to collect more except on account of the royal treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain detailed tribute/accounting records, under oath, with named agents and quantities; these declarations are to be used to adjust salaries and held as evidence for Crown oversight. Notarial procedures were used to record these oaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply financial adjustments: tributes counted toward officials' salaries; penalties for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The governor ordered that 'whatever they have collected from the Indians held by them in encomiendas be understood as counted toward the salaries which his Majesty may have ordered to be paid to them... And they shall do nothing contrary to this, under penalty of five hundred pesos for the exchequer for each person and for each violation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribute previously collected by officials will be offset against their salaries; impose explicit monetary penalties (500 pesos) for unauthorized holding/collection. Officials must present quarterly (each third of the year) before the Excellency for salary disbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use notarial oaths invoking God and the Virgin as formal legal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Notarial practice: oaths taken 'before God and the blessed Mary, with the sign of the cross +, in due legal form; and under this charge he promised to tell the truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record declarations and testimonies via a notary using religiously framed oaths as legally binding statements; witnesses are recorded and documents are signed for Crown records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recover unlawfully sold or seized indigenous persons when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: "a few days ago I went to the island of Cubu to set free some friendly Indians whom some soldiers had seized... It was very difficult to get them back, for they had been sold and were already among the Indians. This cost me no little labor; but... all the Indians were returned to their village at my expense."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act to recover and restore indigenous people unlawfully seized or sold, even at personal/administrative cost, to maintain local goodwill and justice. Report such recoveries and their costs to superiors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance moral/religious aims with colonial expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated appeals to 'our Lord' and the conversion of natives: 'I have faith in God that from this small beginning He will enlarge and increase the kingdoms and seigniories... and we shall be able to carry the true knowledge of the holy Catholic faith to so many barbarous and blinded men...'; and directives to have natives instructed in Catholic tenets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame colonization and conquest as intertwined with missionary objectives; prioritize sending clergy and establishing ecclesiastical structures as part of legitimate colonial policy.
